title: A Springbok Runs 55 MPH, So Why Does It Bounce 6 Feet Up Instead?
subject: springbok

scenes.text: A springbok can run 55 miles an hour. So why does it sometimes bounce instead?
It leaps up to six and a half feet into the air, legs stiff, back bowed, again and again.
It's called pronking, and the whole herd can do it at once.
Mid-leap, it flips open a white flap of hair along its rump and releases a strong scent.
The leading theory: the bounce warns the herd, confuses a predator, or gives a better view of one hiding.
Scientists still argue about it. A springbok can outrun almost anything, and sometimes it jumps instead.

description:
A springbok can run 55 miles an hour, yet sometimes it bounces straight up instead.
Pronking sends it up to six and a half feet, stiff-legged, with a white flap of hair flipped open.
Why do you think it does it? Tell us below.
